title: where it comes from
subtitle: the words you picked up along the way

steps.text: your inner voice didn't come out of nowhere.
as kids, we talk out loud to ourselves while we play and figure things out. slowly, that talk moves inside.
on the way in, it picks up words from the people and places around us.
does your inner voice ever sound like someone you know?

options.label: yes
options.reply: that's common. sometimes we carry someone else's words for a long time.

options.label: no
options.reply: okay. it might be a mix of a lot of places.

options.label: that's a hard one
options.reply: that's okay. you don't have to go there. you can skip anything here, and real help is in settings if you ever want it.

steps.text: a parent's warning. a teacher's red pen. a coach's push. the feed's opinion.
some of those voices were trying to help. some weren't. either way, they don't get to be the only voice you have.

steps.prompt: where might some of your inner voice's words come from?
steps.reply: you don't have to know for sure. just being curious about it gives you a little room.

steps.text: here's the hopeful part: you can add new words, in your own voice.
your inner voice picked up words along the way. you can add new ones.
steps.evidence: a well-known theory of how inner speech develops, not tested as advice

steps.text: today, notice one word your inner voice uses a lot. no need to change it.

grounding.idea: inner speech develops from the out-loud private speech of childhood
